For commercial re-use, please contact journals.permissions@oup.com Abstract Aims The clinical risk profile of atrial fibrillation (AF) patients is different in men and women. Our aim was to identify sex differences in blood biomarkers in patients with paroxysmal AF. Methods and results Sex differences in 92 blood biomarkers were measured in 364 patients included in our discovery cohort, the identification of a risk profile to guide atrial fibrillation therapy (AF-RISK) study, assessed by multivariable logistic regression and enrichment pathway analysis. Findings were subsequently confirmed in 213 patients included in our validation cohort, the Reappraisal of Atrial Fibrillation: Interaction between HyperCoagulability, Electrical remodelling, and Vascular Destabilisation in the Progression of AF (RACE V) study. In the discovery cohort, mean age was 59 ± 12 years, 41% were women. CHA 2 DS 2 -VASc-score was 1.6 ± 1.4. A total of 46% had hypertension, 10% diabetes, and 50% had heart failure, predominantly with preserved ejection fraction (47%). In women, activated leucocyte cell adhesion molecule (ALCAM) and fatty acid binding protein-4 (FABP-4) were higher. In men, matrix metalloproteinase-3 (MMP-3), C-C motif chemokine-16 (CCL-16), and myoglobin were higher. In the validation cohort, four out of five biomarkers could be confirmed: levels of ALCAM ( P = 1.73 × 10 –4 ) and FABP-4 ( P = 2.46 × 10 –7 ) and adhesion biological pathways [false discovery rate (FDR) = 1.23 × 10 –8 ] were higher in women. In men, levels of MMP-3 ( P = 4.31 × 10 –8 ) and myoglobin ( P = 2.10 × 10 –4 ) and markers for extracellular matrix degradation biological pathways (FDR = 3.59 × 10 –9 ) were higher. Conclusion In women with paroxysmal AF, inflammatory biomarkers were more often higher, while in men with paroxysmal AF, biomarkers for vascular remodelling were higher. Our data support the clinical notion that pathophysiological mechanisms in women and men with AF may differ. Trial registration Clinicaltrials.gov identifier NCT01510210 for AF-RISK; Clinicaltrials.gov NCT02726698 for RACE V. Graphical Abstract Atrial fibrillation Blood biomarkers Sex differences Inflammation Vascular disease Dutch Heart Foundation NHS2010B233 What’s new? In patients with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (AF), inflammation biomarkers are more expressed in women in comparison to men, and vascular remodelling biomarkers are more expressed in men in comparison to women. In patients with paroxysmal AF, enrichment of cell adhesion pathways in women compared to men, and enrichment of extracellular matrix organization pathways in men compared to women were observed. Blood biomarker analysis may contribute to a personalized medicine approach in patients with paroxysmal AF.

extracted_data.document_summary: This study aimed to identify and validate sex differences in 92 circulating blood biomarkers in patients with paroxysmal Atrial Fibrillation (AF) using discovery (AF-RISK) and validation (RACE V) cohorts. Key findings consistently reveal that inflammatory biomarkers, specifically Activated leucocyte cell adhesion molecule (ALCAM) and Fatty acid binding protein-4 (FABP-4), are higher in women. Conversely, biomarkers associated with vascular remodelling, such as Matrix metalloproteinase-3 (MMP-3) and Myoglobin, are consistently higher in men. C-C motif chemokine-16 (CCL-16) was higher in men in the discovery cohort but not confirmed in the validation cohort. These findings suggest distinct pathophysiological mechanisms between sexes in AF.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study on sex differences in circulating blood biomarkers in patients with paroxysmal Atrial Fibrillation (AF).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational study, not involving therapeutic interventions, activities, or dose comparisons. Blood sampling was performed in patients with paroxysmal AF in sinus rhythm. A total of 92 circulating blood biomarkers were initially measured using multiplex immunoassay (Olink proximity extension assay technology from the cardiovascular panel III); 88 were included for analysis after excluding four biomarkers with detection issues. Biomarker levels were expressed as normalized protein expression on a log2-transformed concentration, and statistical analysis was adjusted for confounders such as obesity, age, and heart failure. Patients were characterized as having paroxysmal, self-terminating AF, implying less severe remodeling.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Cell adhesion molecule involved in leukocyte recruitment during tissue damage, mediating inflammation and cellular interactions.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Higher in women with paroxysmal Atrial Fibrillation (AF), associated with tissue damage, stroke, and early recurrence after AF ablation.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates heightened inflammatory processes and cell adhesion pathway activity, contributing to distinct pathophysiological mechanisms in women with paroxysmal AF. Also associated with increased thrombogenesis risk, long-term mortality in stroke, and early recurrence after AF ablation.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Oxygen-binding protein in muscle tissue, typically indicates muscle degradation or stress. In this context, it is grouped with markers for vascular remodelling.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Higher in men with paroxysmal AF compared to women.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates vascular remodelling in men with paroxysmal AF. Its release may be due to silent ischemia or subclinical coronary artery disease, and it may also reflect higher muscle mass in men. Its elevation with MMP-3 suggests a significant role of vascular remodelling in AF substrate formation in men.
